title: Epic 10: Operations & Risk Management
description: Monitoring, rollback, and risk mitigation for the gate system. Risks: gate latency (62 gates per transition), false-positive BLOCKs frustrating user, gates drifting from real-world repo behavior, scope creep into 'doing the work' (gates are read-only by contract). Mitigations: most gates read dossier (cached) instead of live gh — only A1/A2/A12/C12/C13 hit live (~5 calls per transition, ~500ms total acceptable); every BLOCK has --override-gate escape hatch with logged reason; 14-day refresh threshold + on-demand @researcher refresh; rigid contract that gates only verify.
design: Risk register: gate latency (mitigated by caching), false-positive BLOCKs (escape hatch + audit), drift (refresh threshold + manual override for institutional knowledge), scope creep (rigid 3-layer contract). Operational invariant: gates never mutate state outside ~/.contribute-system/log.jsonl.
notes:
Rollback strategy: each piece is independent. Disable the gate-runner by removing one line from SKILL.md. Disable a single gate by chmod -x on its script. Memory bank state survives. Per-repo opt-out via disabled_gates dossier field for repos where a gate doesn't apply.
Doc cross-ref: 000-docs/010-OD-RISK-operations-and-risk.md. Per-piece independence verified 2026-05-03: regression test surfaced gh_safe retry-budget bug (false-BLOCK on 404s), fix shipped same session. Override audit trail working (transition.sh --override-gate logs to log.jsonl + candidate frontmatter). Per-repo opt-out via dossier disabled_gates: [...] field.

design: Phase split is opt-in additive — earlier phases keep working when later ones don't exist. Phase 2's plugin manifest is a thin wrapper around Phase 1's filesystem layout. Phase 3's MCP server treats the existing filesystem layout as a degradation fallback when the server is unreachable.

title: Add lifecycle 'dropped' state with reason capture

notes: Dropped reasons accumulate. Useful signal for tuning scout — if multiple candidates from one upstream get dropped for 'maintainer hostile', that's institutional knowledge.

The 'dropped' state already exists in the lifecycle (open → shortlist → claimed → working → submitted → merged | dropped) and reasons are captured via frontmatter dropped_reason: + log.jsonl candidate_dropped event with .details.reason. Reason-capture is already wired (visible in audit-overrides output). A standalone state-transition reason-capture interface would just duplicate what frontmatter already does.

title: Build gate-latency profiler + per-gate timing report
description: The 62-gate budget is ~5 seconds total per transition. Add a profiler that records per-gate wall-clock time on each transition.sh invocation, emits a summary report (gate ID + duration + verdict) to log.jsonl, and flags any gate exceeding 1s as a perf regression.
design: Profiler is a wrapper around the gate execution loop in gate-runner. Adds a duration_ms field to each gate's verdict JSON before logging.
notes: Most gates should be <100ms (read dossier, no live calls). Live-fetching gates (A1/A2/A12/C12/C13) are budgeted ~500ms each. Anything outside budget is a bug or a network issue.
close_reason: DEFERRED — premature for Phase 1. gate-runner already enforces 10s wall-clock timeout per gate (preamble.sh) and 4s timeout on gh_safe network calls. Latency profiler + monitor are valuable when there are >5 users hitting the system concurrently or when median transition >2s. Phase 1 single-user has neither concern. Re-open if /contribute claim takes >10s end-to-end consistently.

title: Document gate severity decision tree (BLOCK vs WARN vs INFORM)
description: Author a 000-docs/ entry that explains when a gate should emit BLOCK vs WARN vs INFORM. Heuristic: BLOCK if proceeding causes irreversible reputation damage (PR posted, maintainer pinged); WARN if it causes inconvenience but is recoverable (lint failure, missing test); INFORM if it's just contextual logging (this repo squash-merges).
design: Decision tree is a flowchart: 'is the action irreversible?' → BLOCK; 'does the user need to know?' → WARN; 'is this just for the audit log?' → INFORM. SKIP is not a severity, it's a not-applicable signal.
notes: Lives at 000-docs/<NNN>-DR-STND-gate-severity-decision-tree.md. The decision tree is the spec for gate authors.
close_reason: Evidence: 000-docs/005-AT-SPEC-gate-inventory.md § Severity levels documents BLOCK / WARN / INFORM / PASS / SKIP with decision criteria. Override mechanism documented in same file.

title: Write remaining ~21 gates (mostly LLM-aided)
description: The 21 remaining gates from the 62-mode catalog: D1 (tone), D7 (tone-match upstream), B15 (dead-ai-code detection), F2 (provenance), and ~17 others. Most require LLM-aided judgment (not pure determinism). Approach: build a llm-judge wrapper that calls Claude with a constrained prompt + structured output, returning the same gate verdict JSON shape.
design: LLM gates are not 'less rigorous' — they have stricter logging requirements (full prompt + full response + verdict in log.jsonl) so verdicts are auditable. Determinism guarantee replaced with reproducibility (same input + same model = same output, modulo LLM nondeterminism).
notes: LLM-aided gates still must obey the gate contract (stdin/stdout JSON, exit 0, <10s). The wrapper handles timeouts + structured-output validation. Cost-controlled by caching gate verdicts per (candidate, dossier-hash) tuple.
close_reason: DEFERRED — empirical-signal-driven. The 21 remaining gates are listed at 000-docs/005-AT-SPEC-gate-inventory.md § Currently installed (41 of 62) marked '(planned)'. Per project plan, gates get built as real failure modes surface in the wild — not preemptively. 41 of 62 covers all observed failure modes from PostHog #55412 and Tracer-Cloud opensre #1129. Build the next gate when the next trap surfaces.

title: Define gate contract reference doc (stdin/stdout JSON schema)
description: Spec for what every gate script must accept on stdin and emit on stdout. Stdin: {candidate: <frontmatter>, dossier: <frontmatter>, action: <transition>}. Stdout: {gate_id: 'A05', verdict: 'BLOCK'|'WARN'|'PASS'|'SKIP'|'INFORM', message: '...', evidence: {...}}. Plus the preamble template (set -e, trap-on-error → emit BLOCK with 'gate crashed', timeout enforcement).
design: Contract is forward-compatible: new keys in stdin/stdout don't break existing gates (they ignore unknown keys). Schema versioning via a stdin.contract_version field.
notes: Lives at 000-docs/<NNN>-DR-STND-gate-contract.md. Should be the canonical reference any gate author follows. Stub gates ship in gates/ with the preamble already applied.
